# 052 Launch saturator/clipper qualification, realtime audit, and benchmark

## Outcome

Qualify the fixed-2x cubic launch saturator after Issue 053 closes its product contract.

## Context

Issue 019 stopped after two attempts and contributes accepted scalar checkpoint `e674d5e` only as
technical input. Issue 053 owns the missing bank/registry/graph product closure. This stateless
qualification issue starts only after Issue 053 passes, follows the accepted launch effect/runtime/
rack/graph contracts, never V1, and permits exactly two attempts: Terra plus one Sol correction.
Timed benchmark count is zero and no benchmark is authorized before every functional/preflight gate
is green.

## Scope

Add the checked independent transfer/alias corpus across launch rates, expanded drive/output/mix and
asymmetric-lane matrices, 10,000 seeded transitions and million-sample finite rows, cohort/tail/
determinism evidence, a 100,000-render realtime audit, native/AArch64/Wasm build and instruction
gates, and audition/listening handoff. Research additional modes, ADAA and quality/factor choices as
nonlaunch comparisons only; they cannot silently alter the accepted Issue-019 scalar or Issue-053
product contract.

## Required public interfaces/contracts

Consume the exact accepted Issue-019 scalar and completed Issue-053 bank/registry/graph artifact.
Qualification reports are deterministic, checksummed and separate from production DSP.

## Deliverables

Corpus/oracles, expanded deterministic matrices, realtime audit, target/instruction records,
benchmark preflight/artifact and listening protocol/results.

## Explicit non-goals

Production DSP redesign, general oversampling/SRC, changing domains/tolerances/latency, true-peak
claims, or blocking unrelated effect implementation.

## Dependencies by exact issue title

- Launch soft-clip bank and graph closure

## Hazards/decisions

Additional modes/factors are research evidence only. A product defect returns to a new bounded
product issue; qualification does not patch it or weaken gates.

## Acceptance gates with objective measurements

All expanded corpus/mutation/realtime/target gates pass. Benchmark tooling proves zero-launch
argument/schema/output/overwrite/shell behavior, then exactly one future invocation runs one warmup
and two measured rounds with no performance threshold or retry. Blinded gain-matched listening is
recorded only after objective candidate freeze.

## Target matrix

Pinned native scalar/AVX2, AArch64 NEON, browser Wasm scalar/simd128 and compile-only fallbacks.

## Required evidence

Candidate commit, corpus hashes, maxima, audit counters, target/instruction records, raw benchmark
JSON and environment, listening records, strict verdict, attempt count and benchmark invocation count.
